name: State of Fitness APIs 2026
methodology: Every field verified against vendor primary sources (developer docs, public repos, registries) by aifitnessapi.com during 2026 and published with per-item provenance on the linked pages. Fields that could not be verified are null — never guessed. No dollar figures by design: prices are volatile; structures are stable.

fields.devCost: How the vendor bills developers: free | free-tier-then-paid | usage-based | contact-sales
fields.userSideCost: What each end user must own or pay for before data flows (null = none documented)
fields.sourceHref: aifitnessapi.com page carrying the verified claims

items.label: Fitbit Web API (Google)
items.userSideCost: Each user must own a Fitbit device and account.
items.approvalGate: Developer app registration; access to other users' intraday data is case-by-case (verify).

items.label: Garmin Health / Activity API
items.userSideCost: Users sync their own Garmin devices; if you supply wearables, Garmin asks for the number of devices when you request the program.
items.approvalGate: Garmin Connect Developer Program approval, for business use only; Garmin confirms an application's status within two business days.

items.label: Oura Cloud API
items.userSideCost: Each user needs an Oura Ring and an active Oura Membership; the API returns 403 when a user's subscription has expired.
items.approvalGate: A new API application is limited to 10 users until Oura approves it, with no limit once approved.

items.label: WHOOP Developer Platform
items.userSideCost: Users authorize your app with their own WHOOP accounts, so they are WHOOP members already.
items.approvalGate: New apps start on a Sandbox tier of 10 members and move up through reviewed tiers of 100, 1,000, 5,000 and unlimited; developers need a WHOOP membership to build.

items.label: Strava API
items.userSideCost: A Strava account whose data your app reads, authorized by the athlete; Standard Tier apps may require specified end users to hold an active Strava subscription.
items.approvalGate: A Strava subscription is a prerequisite for creating an app, which starts in single-player mode; connecting more athletes needs Strava's review.

items.label: Polar Open AccessLink
items.userSideCost: Each user needs a Polar Flow account and must accept all of Polar's mandatory consents; without them, user endpoints return 403.

items.label: Withings Public API
items.userSideCost: Each user needs a Withings device and account; accounts created from October 12, 2026 need Withings+ to share data with a free-plan app.
items.approvalGate: No review is described for the Public API; an app whose callback URL misses Withings' requirements stays in restricted mode, limited to 10 linked users.

items.label: Suunto Cloud API
items.userSideCost: Each user signs in with their Suunto App account, where their Suunto watch syncs its data.
items.approvalGate: Suunto partner program application for companies and organizations, with the API agreement; Suunto replies within two weeks and offers no access for personal use.

items.label: Wahoo Cloud API
items.userSideCost: Each user connects their own Wahoo account; workouts recorded in third-party apps are not shared.
items.approvalGate: Wahoo approves Cloud API requests, and production apps go through a further review for a higher rate limit.

items.label: Apple HealthKit
items.approvalGate: App Store review checks that your health usage-description strings match what you actually do.

items.label: Google Health Connect
items.approvalGate: Play Console health-data declaration and review before you can publish.

items.label: Terra
items.approvalGate: Some providers need a special setup process first; Terra's docs name WHOOP, Dexcom, Huawei, Strava and Virtuagym.

items.label: Rook
items.approvalGate: Dexcom, Samsung Health, Strava and WHOOP need your own developer accounts, which Rook says can take several weeks.

items.label: Spike
items.approvalGate: Sales-assisted onboarding: every plan is bought through a demo call, with a dedicated implementation engineer from sandbox.

items.label: Nutritionix
items.approvalGate: Higher tiers are gated through a Syndigo sales contact rather than a self-serve checkout.

items.label: KinesteX
items.approvalGate: Access runs through a contact form and an issued API key — no self-serve signup.

items.label: Sency (SMKit)
items.approvalGate: Sign-up runs through a contact form that leads to a call, and Sency's Terms of Use put commercial or production use under a separate paid service agreement.

items.label: LLM API (coaching, plan generation, food parsing)
